test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

You said to me, “ I shall reach in time for the concert.”

options.text: You told me that I should reach in time for the concert.
You told me that you shall reach in time for the concert.
You told me that you would reach in time for the concert.
You told me that I would reach in time for the concert.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In reported speech, the future tense** 'shall' **changes to **'would'.**
 
• Since the direct speech is in future tense and uses **'shall**', it should be changed to **'would'** in indirect speech.
 
• Therefore, the correct conversion of the sentence is: "You told me that you would reach in time for the concert".

Hence, the correct statement is '***You told me that you would reach in time for the concert*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In indirect speech, the pronouns and verb tenses are often changed to match the reporting verb and the context of the sentence.
 
• For example,** 'I'** changes to **'you'** if the reporting verb is 'said to me'.
 
• The tense of the verb in the direct speech is shifted back to a past form in indirect speech.
